Mark: breaks at a step
Step: 3
Lines: "Axiom R makes every deed an irreversible record, so a node's net destabilisation can be measured from its accumulated actions and removal is irreversible."
"AP31 establishes that every action is classified as stabilising or destabilising with confidence p computed from accumulated records."
"Minor destabilisation → minor correction. Catastrophic destabilisation → catastrophic correction."
"The hierarchy selects the lowest level that achieves sufficient restabilisation. Removal is never selected when separation suffices. Separation is never selected when restriction suffices."
"The floor F is the destabilisation at which maintaining the node in permanent separation costs more than removal: F ≥ C_sep / B_total."
"Below this floor, Level 4 is always more efficient than Level 5 regardless of organism state."
Place: none
Why: Step 3 does not follow from the line it builds on, or from any line it cites. Axiom R only makes each deed an irreversible record from which that node’s net destabilisation can be measured; it does not follow that every member harms the whole. The paper classifies actions as stabilising or destabilising, scales correction from minor to catastrophic, and selects the lowest level that restabilises, with Level 5 only past a defined floor. “Take it that” every harm passes that floor, and that no lower level is enough for any member, is not given by those lines. The road’s own note that this is added is right, and that failure comes before the brake is ever reached.

result.Lines:
"Axiom R makes every deed an irreversible record, so a node's net destabilisation can be measured from its accumulated actions and removal is irreversible."
"AP31 establishes that every action is classified as stabilising or destabilising with confidence p computed from accumulated records."
"Minor destabilisation → minor correction. Catastrophic destabilisation → catastrophic correction."
"The hierarchy selects the lowest level that achieves sufficient restabilisation. Removal is never selected when separation suffices. Separation is never selected when restriction suffices."
"The floor F is the destabilisation at which maintaining the node in permanent separation costs more than removal: F ≥ C_sep / B_total."
"Below this floor, Level 4 is always more efficient than Level 5 regardless of organism state."
result.Why: Step 3 does not follow from the line it builds on, or from any line it cites. Axiom R only makes each deed an irreversible record from which that node’s net destabilisation can be measured; it does not follow that every member harms the whole. The paper classifies actions as stabilising or destabilising, scales correction from minor to catastrophic, and selects the lowest level that restabilises, with Level 5 only past a defined floor. “Take it that” every harm passes that floor, and that no lower level is enough for any member, is not given by those lines. The road’s own note that this is added is right, and that failure comes before the brake is ever reached.
